headline: KSE-100 eases 0.36% to 177,623.88 as Monday's rate-hold rally cools off, and today's two biggest stories -- PTCL's profit turnaround and the Cabinet's refining-policy nod -- both get sold, not bought.
summary: The index slipped 638 points to 177,623.88, a normal pause after Monday's 4.23% surge, not a reversal. SBP's second straight hold at 11.5% and last week's S&P upgrade to 'B' still favour banks, and oil sitting almost 19% above where it was a month ago keeps E&P in the tailwind seat. But today's two headline stories cut the other way: PTCL swung to a Rs4.7bn profit and its stock still fell, and the Cabinet's refining-policy approval got sold on a contested duty cut. Current-account fragility and a still-live Middle East conflict keep the desk leaning cautious rather than chasing Monday's move.

sectors.name: Banks
sectors.why: T-bill/PIB yields (11.79%/11.69%) sit above the held 11.5% policy rate, the SBP hold removes near-term uncertainty, and last week's S&P upgrade to 'B' is a direct credit-quality tailwind.

sectors.name: E&P / Oil & Gas
sectors.why: Brent is still roughly 19% above where it was a month ago even after today's 1.6% dip -- a structural tailwind for OGDC/PPL/MARI/POL.

sectors.name: Fertilizer
sectors.why: Domestic-demand defensive with low direct oil-import exposure, one of the macro desk's three named favoured groups right now.

sectors.name: Refineries
sectors.why: Today's Brownfield Refining Policy approval (Euro-V mandate, Gulf investor roadshows) is a real medium-term catalyst, but the sector sold off intraday on a contested cut to deemed-duty protection (7.5% to 5%) -- near-term price action argues caution even as the policy backdrop improves.

sectors.name: OMCs
sectors.why: A whipsawing oil tape compounds margin-timing risk on fuel pass-through, and the current account is back in deficit -- a double headwind.

sectors.name: Autos
sectors.why: Imported-input costs plus a still-restrictive policy rate keep demand under pressure, even where individual names look technically strong.

watchlist.angle: The desk's highest-confidence live signal today -- an OBV volume-divergence trigger that has won 96.6% of the time across 89 backtested trades on BML's own history, still 83.3% out-of-sample. Fundamentals back it up: rated 'attractive' (P/E around 6.5, a 32% net margin), and it sits in the banks group the macro desk currently favours. H1 results due 2026-07-31 -- the next real test of the thesis.
watchlist.risk: Pays no dividend, so the return depends entirely on a re-rating; it also trades outside core KSE-100 coverage with thinner liquidity, and the upcoming results could confirm or break the setup either way.

watchlist.angle: Today's biggest single-stock headline: 1HCY26 net profit of Rs4.7bn versus a year-ago loss of Rs9.9bn, revenue up 62% YoY on the Ufone-Telenor amalgamation -- a real, dated, already-confirmed catalyst.
watchlist.risk: The stock fell 1.5% on the day it reported the turnaround, and trailing fundamentals still tag it lossmaking with no dividend -- a textbook 'sell the news' pattern where the market may already have priced the good news, or wants to see it repeat before paying up.

watchlist.angle: Ground zero for today's refining story -- up nearly 3% on roughly 3x normal volume, RSI above 67, directly on the Cabinet's approval of Brownfield Refining Policy amendments. Cheap on paper (P/E around 4.7); H1 results land 2026-08-11, the first hard numbers since the policy news.
watchlist.risk: It's a policy amendment, not an executed investment yet, the sector itself sold off intraday on the same news over the deemed-duty cut, and net margins are thin (around 7%) -- an RSI above 67 also means some of the good news is likely already in the price.

watchlist.angle: A live Donchian-55 breakout trigger fired today -- on TPLT's own history this setup has won 62% of the time across 13 trades, still 75% out-of-sample. It's the only technology-sector name with a live proven-strategy trigger right now.
watchlist.risk: Low-confidence read: only 13 historical trades to judge it on, and there's no fundamental rating or dated catalyst on file to back the technical signal up -- this one stands on the trigger alone.

watchlist.angle: A trend-plus-momentum trigger fired today, and the fundamentals aren't bad for an auto name -- 'mixed' rating, but cheap (P/E around 5.1), forward earnings improving, and a healthy 13% net margin.
watchlist.risk: Autos sit on the macro desk's avoid list (imported-input costs, restrictive policy rate pressuring demand), and the trigger itself is low-confidence -- 55% historical hit rate across 38 trades. A real case of a stock-level signal fighting a sector-level headwind.

catalysts.event: H1CY26 results due: FFC, EFERT and others -- first read on the macro desk's favoured fertilizer group
BML and AKBL H1CY26 results due; also the SBP's weekly FX reserves print and the last day to buy UBL for its confirmed dividend (Rs16.0, ~7.2% yield)
PBS releases July CPI -- the first official print since the recent oil whipsaw (brokerages estimate near 9.1% YoY vs June's 11.1%)
NESTLE goes ex-dividend (Rs213.0, ~2.7% yield); HBL results expected around this window
H1CY26 results: ATRL, NRL -- the first hard numbers since today's refining-policy news
SBP Monetary Policy Committee meeting -- second FY27 rate decision

risks: The Middle East conflict is still live and is the single biggest driver of the desk's geo-risk score (conflict/escalation stress reads 100/100, overall gauge 63/100 'moderate') -- Brent is still up almost 19% on the month despite today's dip, and a fresh escalation could reprice energy and PSX sentiment fast.

External accounts stay fragile: FY26 closed with a $139mn current-account deficit despite record remittances, reserves ($17.26bn) are moving choppily week to week, and the rupee keeps creeping weaker (USD/PKR +0.47% today) -- all reasons SBP stays cautious on any future rate cut.

Today gave two live examples of 'sell the news': PTC fell on a genuine profit turnaround and refiners sold off on their own policy win. When good headlines don't move the tape, it usually means expectations were already priced in -- worth remembering before reading Monday's surge as the new trend.
disclaimer: Research, not advice. The desk generates signals; it does not place orders. Losses are expected.
